title: Geometry of the cube Q_δ: convex, measurable, diameter ≤ √n, volume ≤ 1
statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, δ ≥ 0, and Q_δ := {z ∈ Euclid n : δ < z_i < 1 − δ for all i}. Then Q_δ is convex, Q_δ is measurable, ‖x − y‖ ≤ √n for all x, y ∈ Q_δ, and Lⁿ(Q_δ) ≤ 1 (Lebesgue measure volume, as an element of [0, ∞]).
lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (δ : ℝ), 0 ≤ δ → Convex ℝ {z : Euclid n | ∀ i, δ < z i ∧ z i < 1 - δ} ∧ MeasurableSet {z : Euclid n | ∀ i, δ < z i ∧ z i < 1 - δ} ∧ (∀ x ∈ {z : Euclid n | ∀ i, δ < z i ∧ z i < 1 - δ}, ∀ y ∈ {z : Euclid n | ∀ i, δ < z i ∧ z i < 1 - δ}, ‖x - y‖ ≤ Real.sqrt n) ∧ volume {z : Euclid n | ∀ i, δ < z i ∧ z i < 1 - δ} ≤ 1
